findings.evidence: admin/scratch/003-complete-skill-develop/lane-assignments.json:tasks[14] (T15) anchor_r — T15's `anchor_r` field is `['AC-15']`, but every other task in the lane plan uses an R-anchor (e.g. T1's `['R1']`, T9's `['R9']`). The schema field name `anchor_r` implies an R-level requirement reference; AC-15 is an acceptance criterion, not a requirement. The Gate 3 manifest (lines 25 + 39 + 62-63) documented this as a deliberate exception per finding goal-r1-f1 — T15 anchors to goal Outcome surfaces (c)+(d), not to an R, with the coverage-matrix row reshape making the goal-anchoring explicit. The lane plan correctly cites the exception in T15's `lane_reason` text, but the schema field `anchor_r` is being asked to carry a non-R value, which structurally contradicts its name. Reverse-traceability check (E4): every task in the lane plan must trace to ≥1 R OR a documented goal-anchored exception; T15 has the exception documented but the schema shape is awkward.
findings.claim: Reverse-traceability shape ambiguity — T15's anchor is structurally a goal-Outcome-surface anchor, not an R-anchor, but the lane-assignments.json schema field is named `anchor_r` (singular: R-array). Goal-Driven Execution principle: 'Every AC must trace to ≥1 R, just as every R must be covered by ≥1 AC.' Gate 3 documented T15 as a deliberate exception per goal-r1-f1 — the AC anchors to the goal Outcome (c)+(d) surfaces directly, not to an R. The lane plan respects this in prose but the schema field shape (named `anchor_r`) implies an R-array and the value `['AC-15']` is neither an R nor a goal-Outcome-surface tag. A future reader parsing the lane plan mechanically (e.g. `/insights` Phase 3 reading scratch artefacts, or a downstream `specflow:test` skill computing test coverage) cannot tell from the field shape alone that T15 is the documented orphan-AC exception.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) rename the schema field from `anchor_r` to `anchor` (a more general identifier accepting `R{N}` or `AC-{N}` or `goal-outcome-{x}`), and add a sibling field `anchor_kind: 'requirement' | 'acceptance-criterion' | 'goal-outcome'` so a mechanical reader can disambiguate; OR (b) keep `anchor_r` as-is for the 14 R-anchored tasks AND add an explicit `anchor_exception` field to T15's entry: `anchor_exception: { kind: 'goal-outcome', surfaces: ['c-chat-line-summary', 'd-zero-silent-failures'], gate3_finding: 'goal-r1-f1' }`. Option (a) is a schema-wide change preserving uniformity; option (b) is the surgical addition that preserves the existing field shape for the 14 R-anchored tasks. Either makes the orphan-AC exception structurally readable, not just prose-readable.

findings.evidence: admin/scratch/003-complete-skill-develop/lane-assignments.json — every task entry has a `lane_reason` field describing the four-axis triage tuple, but no entry has an explicit `verify_step` field naming the binary check Phase D + Phase F will exercise to confirm the lane assignment was correct in retrospect. The Gate 3 manifest's calibration notes (line 97) name Goal-Driven as load-bearing on 'binary verification surfaces' — the lane plan's verifiability axis cites the task's acceptance binary, but the lane plan itself is not exercised by any binary check after Phase D completes. A lane plan that ships Green tasks at lane=green and the tasks complete via Yellow-style HITL pairing (because the agent surfaced an unstated complexity) leaves no trace in the lane-assignments.json that the lane was wrong; the corpus signal `/insights` reads later (lane_assigned vs blast_radius_outcome divergence) is captured in `task-history.json`, not the lane plan. The lane plan as written is read-once-and-discarded, not verified-after-execution.
findings.claim: Goal-coverage gap on the lane plan itself — the lane-assignments.json artefact has no binary verify step that exercises the lane assignment after Phase D execution. Every task has a `lane_reason` (the AI's pre-execution judgement) but no `lane_verified_at` or `lane_outcome` field that Phase F can write back when the task closes. The skill's `eval` field (`docs/specflow/admin/scratch/{NNN-slug}-develop/lane-assignments.json exists with one entry per task`) verifies existence + count, not lane-assignment correctness. The corpus signal lives in `task-history.json` per AC-15 of `specflow:develop`'s PRD, but the lane plan itself is not closed-the-loop verified.
findings.proposed_change: Add a `lane_outcome` field to each task entry, populated by Phase F.5 when the task closes (e.g. `lane_outcome: { ran_as_lane: 'green', upgraded_during_run: false, machine_check_failures: 0 }`). The Phase F.5 writer reads each task's actual execution path from the agent's diff + machine-check log and populates the field. The eval line then extends to verify the field is populated for every task. Alternatively (lighter touch), add a single `feature_lane_outcome` field at the lane-assignments.json top level summarising the run: `feature_lane_outcome: { upgrades_fired: 0, machine_check_failures: 0, accept_and_ship_tasks: 0 }`. The lighter touch is the surgical addition; either closes the lane-plan-not-verified-after-execution loop.
